title: AS2 compiler: ActionConstantPool auto-emit for scripts over ~20 unique strings to reduce SWF size and prevent Ruffle push-limit warnings
description:
Task 0879 (in_progress) is tackling this for simple cases. This task is the full story: the AS2 compiler currently pushes ALL strings inline via ActionPush, even when a script has dozens of repeated string constants. Flash Professional always emits ActionConstantPool (0x88) for any script with >= ~5 unique string values.

Ruffle handles inline pushes fine, but:
- Published SWFs are significantly larger (each string repeated verbatim)
- Some real Flash content decompilers assume the pool exists
- When ActionConstantPool index references exceed 255, Ruffle issues warnings

The compiler's string-pool infrastructure exists (see compiler.ts around line 547: 'pool is shared with all sub-compilers so at least one string to pool'). What is missing is the threshold-based auto-promotion: if a DoAction/DoInitAction block accumulates >= N unique strings, emit ActionConstantPool at the top and replace inline strings with pool-index pushes.

Note: coordinate with task 0879 to avoid duplicate work; this task is for the broader auto-emit policy, not the base infrastructure.
